In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coverage of IPTp with SP and ITNs among pregnant women attending ANC in Mozambique was very low, and that stock-outs were frequent.
there is a need to strengthen the supply chain of SP and ITN and that this is a critical step in order to achieve the targets set by the World Health Organization.
this study recommends that the Ministry of Health of Mozambique and its partners should make efforts to improve the supply chain of SP and ITN in the country.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the supply chain is a critical element for the success of any intervention in health care, and should not be overlooked.
the supply chains of IPTp and insecticide-treated nets are critical and should be improved.
the coverage of preventive treatment with SP and ITNs is low in pregnant women and this is mainly due to stock-outs of these commodities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supply chain issues are a major problem in Mozambique and need to be addressed urgently.
supply chain issues are the main barrier for the accomplishment IPTp and ITn coverage targets.
the supply of IPTp and insecticide-treated nets should be a priority in order to improve the coverage of these two interventions.
